_about: The invasion's domains (decided 9 October; bible section 9). The other world is a JRPG world and the rift is where its overworld pushes into ours: a domain is one biome of the classic overworld, its bleed (the tileset the flattened ground paints, DomainGround's: plains, sand, marsh or lava), its wildlife with one tactical signature, and its hero. A rift rolls its domain when it opens, one lead and at most one guest. A pack on the battlefield is one composition on one hex: one sprite (its lead's), one badge (its count), its members listed on a tap (the foes' fresh start, 30 October). compositions are the packs the rift places and sends (the domain's shape on the map), each {id, size, tiers, members}: size is patrol (one or two front types, three to five foes, a detachment's fight), formation (a front and a back, six to sixteen by the tier, the body's fight and the unit the Fractures are counted in), elite (led by a foe flagged elite, the guaranteed curveball a Fracture spawns) or escort (a boss's hand-tailored escort at a tier; none written yet, so the tier's units stand in round robin); tiers lists the tiers (1 to 3) that may deal it, and a tier with none of a size takes the highest tier's under it (every domain needs a tier-one formation and patrol); members are {foe, strength} in order, the first the lead (its sprite and its behaviour; the pack's ring the largest of its members', its pace the slowest, winged only when every member is). The spawn lists by tier are derived (ContentDB.spawn_table: the tier's formations' then patrols' members, each foe once, first seen first) for the harness, the runners and a boss's escort; boss lists the domain's bosses, the slate's first (bible section 9: three a domain before its hero, each battle drawing one its domain has not ended on this run); a domain short of three keeps its old massive stand-in as the last until the slate fills it (30 October); bench names the heroes the campaign's start may deal to this domain, one per campaign, the domain's final (the party, bible section 9: the hero stands in its rank with the domain's wildlife in the other columns). A domain names no map shape: a battle draws its shape by its seed (Ryan, 30 October: "I don't see why the domain should be related to the map type in any way"). Shown to the player: name, flavour. design is internal and never shown: fantasy, signature (what the domain does), answer (how the player beats it, in the engine's own vocabulary). Numbers are placeholders.

entries.name: The Meadow

design.fantasy: The first overworld: grass, round trees, a road that goes nowhere. The invasion's shallow end, and the first thing CARE ever classified. Dragon Quest's plains and Final Fantasy's, where the slime and the goblin live.
design.signature: Numbers that split and swarm. Dumb and many.
design.answer: Area damage, armour against volume, kill order.

entries.flavour: Gate order one: if it is green and it is coming at you, it is not grass.

entries.name: The Waste

design.fantasy: Desert and badlands: sand, dunes, bleached bones, and cacti in rows all facing the same way. The genre's fixed-damage country, where the needles ignore your armour and the thieves take what you have.
design.signature: Fixed damage that no shield answers, and theft of what you have.
design.answer: Hull and tempo over shields; redundancy on the die against theft.

entries.flavour: Field manual, appendix K: the cactus has never been seen to move. Do not take your eyes off the cactus.

entries.name: The Marsh

design.fantasy: Swamp, graveyard, the dungeon: dead trees, tombstones, the poison swamp's purple. The genre's undead, in rusted ornate plate, with the healer who heals them standing behind.
design.signature: Hard to keep down: they regrow, get back up and are called again.
design.answer: Kill order and reach (the healer behind), burst that beats regrow.

entries.flavour: Gate order four: nothing that has died passes the wall. Nothing.

entries.name: The Peak

design.fantasy: Volcano and mountain, the fire cave: lava, black rock, the orange. The genre's bombs and drakes, furious rather than evil, and the mage who throws fire for a living.
design.signature: Hard hits on a telegraph, and heat.
design.answer: Shields for the telegraph, cooling, a lure onto a cold machine.

entries.flavour: Recruitment poster: THEY BROUGHT FIRE. WE BROUGHT BIGGER FIRE.
